doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: Smiley starting out as an entertainer at the Kingfish
summary: They started a dancer who played ukulele at the Kingfish by pushing him onto the floor.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Did you ever work with Smile and Jill?
Oh, he worked with us at Kingfish. Smile and Jill? We started him off in that game.
I used to share him out on the floor. Make him dance. Make him dance. That's right.
Well, he was more of an entertainer then. That's it. That's it. Did he play anything at all?

He was playing a ukulele with me at the Kingfish. Start on the ukulele. We had to push him out on the floor. Make him take that yulele on the floor and dance to go mud. You know, that's what he started off. And he'd tell anybody today. He said, Bill and Dee Dee. Start him in that business. Start him in the business. Dance a little, you know. He could dance a little. Then he'd wake yourself up, wake yourself up. He'd wake up in New York. He's back here somewhere. I don't know. I guess back here. He's in the absence bar.
Yeah, he's in the absence bar. He always did wake most of the absence bar.
